questions.prompt: Do you think photos are the best way to remember something?
questions.sampleA1:
Yes, I like photos.

I have photos of my family.

Photos are good.
questions.sampleA2:
I think photos are good for remembering things.

I have photos from my holiday.

They help me remember the beach and the food.

But sometimes I forget where the photo is from.
questions.sampleB1:
I think photos are a good way to remember things, yes.

Because you can see what happened.

For example, I have photos from my birthday last year, and I remember the party.

However, sometimes photos don't show everything.

You don't remember the smells or the sounds.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'd say photos are one of the best ways, but not the only one. The thing is, a quick snap can bring back a whole day in an instant, which is amazing. That said, I reckon they only capture the surface — they can't really hold onto the sounds, the smells or how you actually felt at the time.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Ha, menga suratlar yoqadi.

Mening oilamning suratlari bor.

Suratlar yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menimcha, fotosuratlar narsalarni eslab qolish uchun yaxshi.

Mening ta'tilimdan olingan fotosuratlarim bor.

Ular menga plyajni va ovqatni eslashga yordam beradi.

Lekin ba'zida fotosurat qayerdan olinganini unutib qo'yaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, suratlar narsalarni eslab qolishning yaxshi usuli, ha.

Chunki siz nima bo'lganini ko'rishingiz mumkin.

Masalan, o'tgan yili tug'ilgan kunimdan suratlarim bor va men o'sha ziyofatni eslayman.

Biroq, ba'zida suratlar hamma narsani ko'rsatmaydi.

Siz hidlarni yoki tovushlarni eslamaysiz.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Xo'sh, menimcha, fotosuratlar voqealarni eslab qolish uchun albatta qimmatli vosita.

Ular vaqtning muayyan bir lahzasining vizual tasvirini taqdim etadi, bu juda kuchli bo'lishi mumkin.

Masalan, eski oilaviy fotosuratlarga qarash kuchli xotiralar va his-tuyg'ularni uyg'otishi mumkin.

Biroq, men ularni *eng yaxshi* usul deb ayta olmayman.

Ba'zan, haqiqiy tajriba va u bilan bog'liq bo'lgan his-tuyg'ular boshqa vositalar, masalan, yozish yoki hatto boshqalar bilan bu haqda gaplashish orqali samaraliroq saqlanadi.

Fotosuratlar vizual narsani aks ettiradi, lekin har doim ham to'liq hikoyani emas.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you think photos are the best way to remember something?
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words - "bir surat ming so'zga tatiydi"
take a trip down memory lane - "xotiralar ko'chasiga sayohat qilmoq (o'tmishni eslash)"
frozen in time - "vaqt ichida muzlab qolgan (saqlanib qolgan damlar)"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I firmly believe that photos are…" - "Ha, men rasmlar haqiqatan ham … ekanligiga ishonaman"
"Looking back at an old photograph can instantly…" - "Eski rasmga qarash bir zumda … ga olib kelishi mumkin"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I firmly believe that photos are one of the best ways to capture memories. They provide a visual record of special moments that our minds gradually forget over time.
Additionally, looking back at an old photograph can instantly trigger strong emotions and transport you right back to that exact day. As people often say, "a picture is worth a thousand words," making it an invaluable tool for preserving history.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men fotosuratlar xotiralarni saqlab qolishning eng yaxshi usullaridan biri ekanligiga qat'iy ishonaman. Ular vaqt o'tishi bilan ongimiz asta-sekin unutadigan maxsus lahzalarning vizual yozuvini taqdim etadi.

Bundan tashqari, eski fotosuratga nazar tashlash bir zumda kuchli his-tuyg'ularni qo'zg'atishi va sizni o'sha kunning o'ziga qaytarishi mumkin. Odamlar ko'pincha aytganidek, "bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi", bu esa uni tariхni saqlash uchun bebaho vositaga aylantiradi.

questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like history. It is good. I learn about kings.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like history. I like learning about old things and old people. It is interesting because I can see how things were different. But sometimes it is boring because there are many dates.
questions.sampleB1: I do enjoy studying history, actually. I think it's important to understand the past to understand the present. For example, learning about wars helps us see why certain countries are the way they are today. However, sometimes I find it difficult to remember all the dates and names.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, I genuinely do. I suppose what I love most is the way it helps you make sense of the present. To be honest, I could happily pore over old battles and empires for hours. The only downside is that all the dates and names can be a bit of a slog to remember.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men tarixni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu yaxshi. Men qirollar haqida o'rganaman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menga tarix yoqadi. Menga eski narsalar va eski odamlar haqida o'rganish yoqadi. Bu qiziqarli, chunki men narsalar qanday boshqacha bo'lganini ko'rishim mumkin. Ammo ba'zida zerikarli, chunki ko'p sanalar bor.
questions.uzSampleB1: Men tarixni o'rganishdan rohatlanaman, aslida. O'ylaymanki, hozirgi zamonni tushunish uchun o'tmishni tushunish muhim. Misol uchun, urushlar haqida bilish, nega ayrim davlatlar bugungi kunda shunday ekanligini ko'rishga yordam beradi. Biroq, ba'zida barcha sanalar va nomlarni eslab qolish men uchun qiyin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ha, men tarixni o'rganishni juda yoqtiraman, garchi ba'zida qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Menimcha, hozirgi jamiyat tuzilmalari va siyosiy vaziyatlarni chuqurroq tushunish uchun tarixiy voqealarni o'rganish juda muhim.
Qolaversa, turli madaniyatlar va ularning tarixiy yo'nalishlarini o'rganish insonning dunyoqarashini kengaytiradi va hamdardlikni rivojlantiradi. Muayyan sanalar va shaxslarni yodlash zerikarli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, tarixni o'rganishdan olingan umumiy tushunchalar juda qimmatlidir.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you enjoy studying history?
idioms: history repeats itself - "tarix takrorlanadi"
turn back the clock - "vaqtni orqaga qaytarmoq"
a thing of the past - "o'tmishda qolgan narsa"
sentenceStarters: "Absolutely, I find studying history to be…" - "Mutlaqo, men tarixni o'rganishni … deb bilaman"
"Exploring ancient civilizations and understanding how…" - "Qadimgi sivilizatsiyalarni o'rganish va … tushunish"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Absolutely, I find studying history to be incredibly fascinating. Exploring ancient civilizations and understanding how our modern society was formed gives me a profound sense of perspective.
Learning about the successes and failures of our ancestors is not only interesting but also highly educational. It helps us avoid repeating the same mistakes because, as the saying goes, "history repeats itself" if we do not learn from it.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Albatta, tarixni o'rganish men uchun juda qiziqarli. Qadimgi sivilizatsiyalarni o'rganish va zamonaviy jamiyatimiz qanday shakllanganini tushunish menga chuqur nuqtai nazar beradi.

Ajdodlarimizning muvaffaqiyatlari va muvaffaqiyatsizliklari haqida bilish nafaqat qiziqarli, balki juda ham ibratli. Bu bizga xatolarni takrorlamaslikka yordam beradi, chunki maqolda aytilganidek, agar undan saboq olmasak, "tarix takrorlanadi".

questions.prompt: Do you think shoes are a good gift?
questions.sampleA1: Yes, shoes good. I like shoes. My shoes are blue.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I think shoes are a good gift. Because everyone needs shoes. And you can wear them outside. But maybe not everyone likes the same shoes.
questions.sampleB1: I think shoes can be a good gift, but it depends. If you know the person very well, you can choose a good pair of shoes for them. For example, if your friend likes running, you can buy running shoes. However, if you don't know their style, it's probably better to buy something else.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, it depends. I suppose shoes can be a lovely gift if you know the person inside out — their size, their taste, everything. The thing is, it's a bit of a risky move, because if the fit is off, they'll just end up gathering dust in the wardrobe. So personally, I'd only go for it if I were absolutely sure.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha, poyabzal yaxshi. Menga poyabzal yoqadi. Mening poyabzallarim ko'k.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menimcha poyabzal yaxshi sovg'a. Chunki hammaga poyabzal kerak. Va ularni tashqarida kiyish mumkin. Lekin balki hamma ham bir xil poyabzalni yoqtirmas.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, poyabzal yaxshi sovg'a bo'lishi mumkin, lekin bu narsaga bog'liq. Agar siz odamni juda yaxshi bilsangiz, u uchun yaxshi poyabzal tanlashingiz mumkin.
Masalan, agar do'stingiz yugurishni yoqtirsa, siz unga yugurish poyabzallarini sotib olishingiz mumkin.
Biroq, agar siz ularning uslubini bilmasangiz, boshqa narsa sotib olganingiz yaxshiroq bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Poyabzal o'ylab topilgan sovg'a bo'lishi mumkin, agar siz oluvchining xohishlari va o'lchamlari bilan yaxshi tanish bo'lsangiz. Amaliy va zamonaviy poyabzal juftligi albatta qadrlanishi mumkin. Biroq, bu ham potentsial xavfli tanlovdir. Moslashuv va uslubning subyektiv tabiatini hisobga olsak, mos kelmaydigan narsani tanlash xavfi katta, bu esa umidsizlikka olib kelishi mumkin. Shuning uchun, yaxshi tanlangan poyabzal juftligi ajoyib sovg'a bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, ehtiyotkorlik bilan harakat qilish va agar ishonchingiz komil bo'lmasa, boshqa variantlarni ko'rib chiqish juda muhim.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you think shoes are a good gift?
idioms: better safe than sorry - "keyin afsuslangandan ko'ra hozir ehtiyot bo'lgan yaxshi"
put yourself in someone's shoes - "o'zingizni boshqaning o'rniga qo'yib ko'ring (to'g'ridan-to'g'ri aloqasi yo'q, lekin so'z o'yini sifatida qiziq)"
if the shoe fits, wear it - "agar bu gap sizga tegishli bo'lsa, qabul qiling (yana bir 'shoe' qatnashgan ibora)"
sentenceStarters: "I think shoes can be a wonderfully practical gift, especially if…" - "Fikrimcha, oyoq kiyimlar ajoyib amaliy sovg'a bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa agar…"
"However, buying shoes for someone else can be quite risky since…" - "Biroq, boshqa birovga oyoq kiyim sotib olish ancha qaltis bo'lishi mumkin, chunki…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I think shoes can be a wonderfully practical gift, especially if you know the person’s exact size and taste. High-quality footwear is something everyone needs on a daily basis.
However, buying shoes for someone else can be quite risky since comfort and fit are highly subjective preferences. If you get it wrong, it might end up just gathering dust in the closet, so "it's better to be safe than sorry" and perhaps give a gift card instead.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, poyabzal ajoyib amaliy sovg'a bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa, agar siz odamning aniq o'lchami va didini bilsangiz. Yuqori sifatli poyabzal har kimga har kuni kerak bo'ladigan narsa.

Biroq, boshqa birovga poyabzal sotib olish juda xavfli bo'lishi mumkin, chunki qulaylik va moslik juda subyektiv afzalliklardir. Agar siz adashsangiz, u shkafda chang bosib yotishi mumkin, shuning uchun "ehtiyotkorlik zarar keltirmaydi" va balki uning o'rniga sovg'a kartasini bergan ma'qul.

questions.sampleA1: This is city. Many buildings. And this is forest. Trees.
questions.sampleA2: I see a city. It is big and has tall buildings. And I see trees and people walking. It is nature, I think.
questions.sampleB1: The first picture shows a city. It looks very modern and busy. There are lots of buildings and people. The second picture is different. It's nature, with trees and people walking. I think they are hiking. It's much quieter than the city.
questions.sampleB2: So in the first picture, I can see a group of four young tourists soaking up the buzz of a bustling city at dusk. They've got backpacks on and they're huddled round a phone, with glowing neon signs saying 'City Explorers' and towering glass skyscrapers behind them. The second one, though, is worlds apart. Here four hikers are making their way up a mountain trail, surrounded by pine forest with a river and mountains in the distance. One lad's pointing at the view. Basically, it's the hustle and bustle of the city versus the great outdoors.
questions.uzSampleA1: Bu shahar. Ko'p binolar. Va bu o'rmon. Daraxtlar.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men bir shaharni ko'ryapman. U katta va baland binolari bor. Va men daraxtlar va odamlarni piyoda yurganini ko'ryapman. Bu tabiat, deb o'ylayman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Birinchi rasmda shahar ko'rsatilgan. U juda zamonaviy va gavjumga o'xshaydi. Ko'plab binolar va odamlar bor. Ikkinchi rasm boshqacha. Bu tabiat, daraxtlar va odamlar sayr qilib yurishibdi. Menimcha, ular piyoda sayr qilishyapti. U shahardan ancha tinchroq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda zamonaviy arxitektura va umumiy faollik hissi bilan ajralib turadigan jonli shahar manzarasi tasvirlangan. Bu mashhur sayyohlik maskani bo'lib tuyuladi.
Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda tabiiy landshaft ko'rsatilgan, unda odamlar o'rmon yoki parkga o'xshash joyda sayr qilmoqda. U tinchroq va dam olish muhitini namoyish etadi. Ikkala rasm o'rtasidagi farq odamlarning bo'sh vaqtlarini qanday o'tkazishni tanlash usullarini, shaharda yoki tabiat qo'ynida o'tkazishni ko'rsatadi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Describe these pictures
idioms: the concrete jungle - "beton changalzor (katta shaharni ifodalash uchun)"
the great outdoors - "keng tabiat qo'yni"
miles apart - "bir-biridan juda uzoq (mutlaqo farq qiluvchi)"
sentenceStarters: "The first picture shows a bustling modern city with…" - "Birinchi rasmda … bo'lgan gavjum zamonaviy shahar ko'rsatilgan"
"In stark contrast, the second picture displays…" - "Bunga butkul ziddiyat o'laroq, ikkinchi rasmda … ko'rsatilgan"

questions.sampleAnswer:
The first picture shows a bustling modern city with towering skyscrapers and tourists exploring the urban landscape. The focus here is clearly on urban tourism, architecture, and the fast-paced city life.
In stark contrast, the second picture displays a group of hikers walking through a serene natural environment. They are surrounded by lush greenery, escaping the city to fully immerse themselves in nature. The images highlight two completely different styles of recreation: seeking excitement in the concrete jungle versus finding peace in the great outdoors.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda baland osmono'par binolar va shahar landshaftini o'rganayotgan sayyohlar bilan gavjum zamonaviy shahar tasvirlangan. Bu yerda asosiy e'tibor shahar turizmi, arxitektura va tez sur'atlar bilan davom etayotgan shahar hayotiga qaratilgan.

Keskin farq o'laroq, ikkinchi rasmda bir guruh sayyohlar sokin tabiiy muhit bo'ylab sayr qilayotgani aks etgan. Ular shahardan qochib, yam-yashil o'simliklar bilan o'ralgan holda tabiatga to'liq sho'ng'ishmoqda. Rasmlar dam olishning ikki butunlay boshqa uslubini ta'kidlaydi: beton o'rmonda hayajon izlash va ajoyib tabiat qo'ynida tinchlik topish.

questions.prompt: Why are many young people nowadays interested in traveling to modern cities?
questions.sampleA1: I like city. City is fun. Many people.
questions.sampleA2: I think young people like cities because they are exciting. There are many shops and restaurants. And it is easy to go places because there is a bus. But cities are also expensive.
questions.sampleB1: I think many young people like to travel to modern cities because there are lots of things to do. For example, there are museums and concerts. Also, it's easier to get around because they have good public transport. However, cities can be crowded and expensive, but young people still like them.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I suppose the main pull is the sheer energy of it all. The thing is, modern cities are buzzing with nightlife, shopping and world-class food, which younger people find hard to resist. On top of that, they're keen to snap the famous landmarks they've come across on social media. For them, a city break basically ticks every box.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga shahar yoqadi. Shahar qiziqarli. Ko'p odamlar bor.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, yoshlar shaharlarni yaxshi ko'radilar, chunki ular qiziqarli. U yerda ko'plab do'konlar va restoranlar bor. Va u yerga borish oson, chunki avtobus bor. Lekin shaharlar ham qimmat.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, ko'p yoshlar zamonaviy shaharlarga sayohat qilishni yaxshi ko'radilar, chunki u yerda qilinadigan ko'p narsalar bor. Misol uchun, muzeylar va konsertlar bor. Bundan tashqari, u yerda yurish osonroq, chunki ularda yaxshi jamoat transporti bor. Biroq, shaharlar gavjum va qimmat bo'lishi mumkin, lekin yoshlar ularni baribir yaxshi ko'radilar.
questions.uzSampleB2: Zamonaviy shaharlar bugungi kunda yoshlar uchun katta qiziqish uyg'otadi va menimcha, buning bir nechta asosiy sabablari bor. Birinchidan, bu shaharlar imkoniyatlarni anglatadi – ham kasbiy, ham shaxsiy. Ularda ko'pincha ish o'rinlari va ta'lim muassasalari ko'proq bo'ladi. Ikkinchidan, zamonaviy shaharlar xilma-xil madaniy tajribani taklif etadi. Siz butun dunyodan odamlarni topishingiz mumkin, bu esa fikri ochiq va turli madaniyatlar haqida bilishni istagan yoshlar uchun juda jozibali. Nihoyat, zamonaviy shaharlarning tez sur'atdagi muhiti va doimiy innovatsiyalari yangi tajribalar va dinamik turmush tarzini izlayotganlar uchun ayniqsa hayajonli.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Young people traveling to modern cities
idioms: the sky is the limit - "imkoniyatlarning chegarasi yo'q"
bright lights, big city - "yorqin chiroqlar, katta shahar (shaharning jozibasini ifodalaydi)"
the hustle and bustle - "shovqin-suron va shov-shuv (gavjum shaharning muhiti)"
sentenceStarters: "There are several reasons why modern cities are…" - "Zamonaviy shaharlar … bo'lishining bir qator sabablari bor"
"Firstly, urban centers are hubs of…" - "Birinchidan, shahar markazlari … o'choqlaridir"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several reasons why modern cities are incredibly attractive to younger generations. Firstly, urban centers are hubs of culture, entertainment, and innovation. Young people are naturally drawn to the vibrant nightlife, world-class restaurants, and countless cultural events that only a metropolis can provide.
Secondly, traveling to a modern city is highly convenient. Infrastructure like public transportation makes sightseeing easy, and discovering famous landmarks they have seen on social media is a big draw. They want to experience that cosmopolitan lifestyle firsthand.
Ultimately, modern cities offer a sense of endless possibility. The energy of the crowd and the architectural marvels make city breaks immensely popular because, for adventurous youth, "the sky is the limit" when exploring a new urban destination.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Nima uchun zamonaviy shaharlar yosh avlodlar uchun juda jozibali ekanligining bir nechta sabablari bor. Birinchidan, shahar markazlari madaniyat, ko'ngilochar va innovatsiya markazlaridir. Yoshlar, tabiiyki, faqat metropolislarda mavjud bo'lgan jonli tungi hayot, jahon darajasidagi restoranlar va son-sanoqsiz madaniy tadbirlarga intilishadi.
Ikkinchidan, zamonaviy shaharga sayohat qilish juda qulay. Jamoat transporti kabi infratuzilma diqqatga sazovor joylarni tomosha qilishni osonlashtiradi va ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda ko'rgan mashhur diqqatga sazovor joylarni kashf qilish katta turtki beradi. Ular o'sha kosmopolit turmush tarzini bevosita his qilishni xohlashadi.
Nihoyat, zamonaviy shaharlar cheksiz imkoniyatlar tuyg'usini taqdim etadi. Olomonning energiyasi va me'moriy mo''jizalar shahar sayohatlarini juda mashhur qiladi, chunki sarguzashtli yoshlar uchun yangi shahar yo'nalishini o'rganishda "osmon - chegara"dir.

questions.prompt: Does organizing trips to nature have a positive effect on mental health?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. Nature good. I like trees. Happy.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I think so. Nature is nice and quiet. I like to walk in the forest because it is beautiful. And I feel good.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I think organizing trips to nature is good for mental health. In my opinion, it helps people relax and forget about their problems. For example, when you go to the mountains, you can see beautiful views and breathe fresh air. However, it's important to be prepared and safe.
questions.sampleB2: Absolutely, without a doubt. To be honest, our fast-paced lives take a real toll on us, so getting away into nature is like pressing a reset button. The thing is, fresh air and green surroundings genuinely help you clear your head and unwind. I reckon even a short hike can work wonders for your mood.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Tabiat yaxshi. Men daraxtlarni yaxshi ko'raman. Xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men shunday deb o'ylayman. Tabiat yaxshi va tinch. Men o'rmonda sayr qilishni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki u go'zal. Va men o'zimni yaxshi his qilaman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ha, menimcha tabiatga sayohatlarni tashkil qilish ruhiy salomatlik uchun foydali. Mening fikrimcha, bu odamlarga dam olishga va muammolarini unutishga yordam beradi. Misol uchun, tog'larga borganingizda, chiroyli manzaralarni ko'rishingiz va toza havoda nafas olishingiz mumkin. Biroq, tayyor bo'lish va xavfsizlikni ta'minlash muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men tabiatga sayohatlarni tashkil qilish ruhiy salomatlikka ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatishiga shubhasiz ishonaman. Bugungi tez sur'atlar bilan rivojlanayotgan dunyoda odamlar ko'pincha stress va texnologiyalar bilan haddan tashqari yuklangan. Tabiiy muhitlarga qochish juda zarur bo'lgan tanaffus va aloqani uzish imkoniyatini berishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatdiki, ochiq havoda vaqt o'tkazish xavotirni kamaytiradi va kayfiyatni yaxshilaydi. Bu odamlarga o'zlari bilan qayta bog'lanish va tabiatning osoyishtaligida tinchlik topishga imkon beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Nature trips and mental health
idioms: take a toll on - "zarar yetkazmoq / salbiy ta'sir qilmoq"
clear one's head - "miyani (fikrlarni) tozalash"
nature is the best physician - "tabiat eng yaxshi tabibdir"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, without a doubt, organizing trips to nature has…" - "Ha, shubhasiz, tabiatga sayohat uyushtirish … ga ega"
"Escaping to nature provides a…" - "Tabiat qo'yniga qochish … ni ta'minlaydi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, without a doubt, organizing trips to nature has a profoundly positive impact on mental well-being. Modern life is filled with screens, notifications, and stress, which inevitably takes a toll on our minds. Escaping to nature provides a digital detox that allows the brain to rest.
Moreover, scientific studies have shown that spending time in green spaces significantly lowers cortisol levels, which reduces anxiety and depression. Breathing in fresh air and enjoying the tranquil surroundings helps people clear their heads.
Furthermore, nature walks usually involve physical exertion, which releases endorphins, the body's natural mood elevators. Connecting with the natural world is essentially a way to recharge one's batteries, proving that "nature is the best physician."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, shubhasiz, tabiatga sayohatlarni tashkil qilish ruhiy salomatlikka juda ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatadi. Zamonaviy hayot ekranlar, bildirishnomalar va stressga to'la, bu esa, albatta, bizning ongimizga ta'sir qiladi. Tabiatga qochish miyaga dam berishga imkon beradigan raqamli detoksni ta'minlaydi.

Bundan tashqari, ilmiy tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatdiki, yashil hududlarda vaqt o'tkazish kortizol darajasini sezilarli darajada pasaytiradi, bu esa xavotir va depressiyani kamaytiradi. Toza havoda nafas olish va sokin muhitdan bahramand bo'lish odamlarga ongini tozalashga yordam beradi.

Bundan tashqari, tabiatda sayr qilish odatda jismoniy zo'riqishni o'z ichiga oladi, bu esa tananing tabiiy kayfiyat ko'taruvchilari bo'lgan endorfinlarni chiqaradi. Tabiiy dunyo bilan bog'lanish, asosan, o'z kuchini tiklash usuli bo'lib, "tabiat eng yaxshi tabib" ekanligini isbotlaydi.

questions.sampleA2: I had a problem. My bike was broken. I used a rope and fixed it. And I could ride my bike again. It was good because I needed to go to the shop.
questions.sampleB1: Once, I had a problem with my computer. It wouldn't turn on. I tried restarting it, but it didn't work. I then thought maybe the power cord was broken, so I used a different one from another device. It worked! I was happy because I didn't have to buy a new computer.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so let me tell you about a time I had to think on my feet. Last year I was helping organise a charity event at my college, and about an hour before it kicked off, the projector we'd hired for the main presentation simply packed in. To be honest, I panicked for a second, because all our slides and videos were stuck on it. But then it hit me — nearly everyone in the room had a smartphone. So instead of one big screen, I quickly uploaded the whole presentation to a shared link and had people follow along on their own phones, while I talked them through it. It was a bit rough around the edges, but honestly, it turned out to be even more engaging than the original plan, because everyone was glued to their screens. Now, in terms of my confidence, that moment was a real turning point. The thing is, before that, I always assumed you needed the 'proper' tools to pull something off. Afterwards, I realised that thinking outside the box is a skill you can actually rely on when your back's against the wall. It gave me the courage to come up with unconventional solutions rather than freezing up. You see, as for society, I firmly believe we've got to nurture creativity from an early age. The big challenges we face — climate change, disease, you name it — won't be cracked with old ways of thinking. If we encourage people to experiment and, crucially, to not be afraid of failing, that's where real innovation comes from. After all, necessity is the mother of invention.

bulletPoints: Describe a situation where you solved a problem in a creative way.
How did this solution affect your confidence in thinking differently?
Why is it important for society to nurture creativity and innovation?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A creative problem-solving situation:
I vividly remember a time during a university group project when our primary mapping software unexpectedly crashed just hours before our final presentation. Instead of panicking, I creatively suggested we use an open-source video game creation tool to build a 3D interactive model of our geographic data. It was highly unconventional, but it created an immersive visual experience that amazed the professors.
How it affected my confidence:
That experience massively boosted my confidence. It taught me not to freeze when faced with unexpected obstacles. I realized that thinking outside the box isn't just a buzzword; it's a practical skill. It showed me that sometimes, unconventional tools can produce far superior results than standard procedures.
Why nurturing creativity in society is important:
I believe society must actively nurture innovation because the challenges we face today—like climate change and resource scarcity—cannot be solved with yesterday's logic. Fostering a culture of creativity ensures that people are not afraid to experiment and fail. Progress depends on pushing boundaries, because as Albert Einstein said, "imagination is more important than knowledge."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ijodiy muammolarni hal qilish vaziyati:

Universitetdagi guruh loyihasi vaqtida asosiy xaritalash dasturimiz yakuniy taqdimotdan bir necha soat oldin kutilmaganda ishdan chiqqanini juda yaxshi eslayman. Sarosimaga tushish o'rniga, men ijodiy yondashib, geografik ma'lumotlarimizning 3D interaktiv modelini yaratish uchun ochiq manbali video o'yin yaratish vositasidan foydalanishni taklif qildim. Bu juda noodatiy edi, lekin u professorlarni hayratga solgan immersiv vizual tajribani yaratdi.

Bu mening ishonchimga qanday ta'sir qildi:

Bu tajriba mening ishonchimni juda oshirdi. Bu meni kutilmagan to'siqlarga duch kelganda muzlab qolmaslikka o'rgatdi. Men "standartdan tashqari fikrlash" shunchaki moda so'z emas, balki amaliy ko'nikma ekanligini angladim. Bu menga ba'zan noodatiy vositalar standart protseduralarga qaraganda ancha yaxshi natijalarni berishi mumkinligini ko'rsatdi.

Nima uchun jamiyatda ijodkorlikni rivojlantirish muhim:

Menimcha, jamiyat innovatsiyalarni faol ravishda rivojlantirishi kerak, chunki biz bugungi kunda duch kelayotgan muammolar - iqlim o'zgarishi va resurslarning kamayishi kabi muammolarni kechagi mantiq bilan hal qilib bo'lmaydi. Ijodkorlik madaniyatini rivojlantirish odamlarning tajriba o'tkazishdan va muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrashdan qo'rqmasligini ta'minlaydi. Taraqqiyot chegaralarni surishga bog'liq, chunki Albert Eynshteyn aytganidek, "tasavvur bilimdan muhimroqdir".

questions.prompt: Social media has a strong influence on young people’s behavior and opinions.
questions.sampleA1: Yes. Social media... young people... like it. I like it too. It is fun.
questions.sampleA2: I think social media is okay. I use it every day. I like to see my friends. But sometimes it is bad because people are mean online.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think social media does influence young people a lot. For example, many teenagers spend hours on TikTok and Instagram every day. In my opinion, this can be good because they can connect with friends and learn new things. However, it can also be bad because they might compare themselves to others and feel insecure.
questions.sampleB2: Right, this is a topic I feel quite strongly about, and honestly, I think it's a bit of a double-edged sword. On the one hand, there's no denying that social media has done a lot of good. The thing is, it lets young people connect with friends and communities right across the globe, which gives them a real sense of belonging. On top of that, it's an incredible way to keep up with the news, pick up new skills, and share their own creativity with a massive audience. For a lot of teenagers, it's basically opened doors that simply weren't there before. That said, I do think we have to be careful, because there's a darker side to it. To be honest, the biggest issue for me is how highly addictive these platforms are. It's so easy to go down the rabbit hole and waste hours scrolling. What's more, a lot of what you see is heavily filtered and unrealistic, so young people end up comparing themselves to others and feeling insecure. And of course, there's the whole problem of fake news spreading like wildfire, which means you really have to take everything with a pinch of salt. So where do I stand? Well, on balance, I'd say social media itself isn't the enemy — it's how we use it that matters. I firmly believe the answer lies in digital literacy: if we teach young people to think critically and set healthy boundaries, they can enjoy the benefits while steering clear of the pitfalls. At the end of the day, it's all about balance.

Mening fikrimcha, bu yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin, chunki ular do'stlari bilan bog'lanishlari va yangi narsalarni o'rganishlari mumkin. Biroq, bu yomon ham bo'lishi mumkin, chunki ular o'zlarini boshqalar bilan solishtirib, o'zlarini ishonchsiz his qilishlari mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar, shubhasiz, yoshlarning qarashlari va xatti-harakatlariga sezilarli ta'sir ko'rsatadi. Bir tomondan, u o'zini ifoda etish uchun platforma taqdim etadi va ularga global tendentsiyalar va hamjamiyatlar bilan aloqada bo'lish imkonini beradi, bu esa mansublik hissini uyg'otadi. Biroq, onlayn kontentning saralangan tabiati ko'pincha norealistik umidlarga olib keladi va tana obrazi bilan bog'liq muammolar va ijtimoiy xavotirlik kabi masalalarga hissa qo'shishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, doimiy ravishda ma'lumotga, ham to'g'ri, ham noto'g'ri ma'lumotga duchor bo'lish, tanqidiy fikrlash qobiliyatlarini talab qiladi, bu ko'nikmalarni ko'plab yoshlar hali ham rivojlantirmoqda. Shuning uchun, ijtimoiy tarmoqlar ko'plab afzalliklarni taqdim etsa-da, u jiddiy e'tibor va mas'uliyatli foydalanishni talab qiladigan muhim muammolarni ham keltirib chiqaradi.

questions.sampleAnswer:
The impact of social media on the younger generation is a highly controversial issue. Proponents argue that its influence is largely positive. It serves as an unprecedented global network, allowing youths to connect with peers worldwide effortlessly. Furthermore, platforms like Twitter and TikTok provide instantaneous access to break-neck news, while simultaneously acting as a democratic stage for teenagers to showcase their art, ideas, and creativity to a global audience.
Conversely, critics highlight the severely detrimental effects of these platforms. The most obvious issue is the highly addictive nature of endless scrolling, which wastes valuable time and distracts from studies. Additionally, the rampant spread of misinformation can warp young, impressionable minds. Most worryingly, the constant exposure to curated, unrealistic lifestyles negatively impacts self-esteem, leading to anxiety and depression.
Ultimately, while social media is an immensely powerful tool, it is a "double-edged sword." I believe its benefits can only be harnessed if we teach digital literacy and encourage healthy, moderate consumption to protect young people's mental health.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ijtimoiy tarmoqlarning yosh avlod xulq-atvoriga ta'siri juda bahsli masala. Tarafdorlar uning ta'siri asosan ijobiy ekanligini ta'kidlaydilar. U yoshlarga butun dunyo bo'ylab tengdoshlari bilan oson aloqa qilish imkonini beruvchi misli ko'rilmagan global tarmoq vazifasini o'taydi. Bundan tashqari, Twitter va TikTok kabi platformalar tezkor yangiliklarga darhol kirishni ta'minlaydi, shu bilan birga o'smirlar uchun o'z san'ati, g'oyalari va ijodini global auditoriyaga namoyish etish uchun demokratik sahna bo'lib xizmat qiladi.

Aksincha, tanqidchilar ushbu platformalarning jiddiy zararli ta'sirini ta'kidlaydilar. Eng aniq muammo - bu cheksiz aylantirishning juda o'rganib qolish xususiyati bo'lib, u qimmatli vaqtni behuda sarflaydi va o'qishdan chalg'itadi. Bundan tashqari, noto'g'ri ma'lumotlarning keng tarqalishi yosh, ta'sirchan ongni buzishi mumkin. Eng tashvishlisi, doimiy ravishda saralangan, noreal hayot tarziga ta'sir qilish o'z-o'zini qadrlashga salbiy ta'sir qiladi, bu esa xavotir va depressiyaga olib keladi.

Yakuniy xulosa shuki, ijtimoiy media juda kuchli vosita bo'lsa-da, u "ikki tomonlama tig'li qilichdir". Menimcha, uning afzalliklaridan faqatgina raqamli savodxonlikni o'rgatsak va yoshlarning ruhiy salomatligini himoya qilish uchun sog'lom, me'yoriy iste'molni rag'batlantirsakgina foydalanish mumkin.
